layer_note: Sivavakkiyar's chapter is method, and most of its breath vocabulary is plain: மூலநாடி, வாசி, அனல், அமுதம், பிராணன் are named, so the breath layer is usually as certain as the literal one. Keys are needed only for the counts (எட்டெட்டு), the doors and bolts (வாசல் மூன்று, மூன்று தாள்), the middle (நடு) and the letters (சீ, அவ், யவ்). The social layer is thin and confined to the amulet (1389), the other town (1390) and wandering the land (1402).

literal.reading: Bound up with a potsherd as a charm, the mantra is a mere device: will the Maker live in it? Set the air that moves within the eight and eight and eight in the circled letter ய and come to know it.

breath.reading: The breath, moving through counted stations (eight, eight and eight: breath counts or the cells of a drawn centre), is to be fixed in the letter ய drawn in a circle, as on a yantra.

social.reading: Against the amulet: a mantra written and tied up with a shard cannot hold the Lord.

literal.reading: Saying 'he is not in this town', where do you run? How would the Lord live in that other town? Know the Lord who dwells in the six within the final hollow, in the final சி and அ.

breath.reading: The six in the hollow are the six centres of the body, where the Lord is to be known instead of in another town.

consciousness.reading: The Lord is known in the letters சி and அ, which the five-syllable key reads as Siva and the soul: he is found where the two meet.

social.reading: Against travel to another town to find the Lord: pilgrimage misplaces him.

literal.reading: Obscure: within you is the hymn set by the filling; if skin, eye, tongue and nose are gathered round it, the one who wears rudraksha and konrai dances in the hall, and the great light will not speak of it afterwards.

breath.reading: பூரியிட்ட may be the in-breath (பூரகம்); with the four senses drawn round it, the dance is seen in the inner hall: breath and withdrawal of the senses as the condition of the vision.

consciousness.reading: What is seen in the light cannot be told afterwards.

literal.reading: Fools fix their eyes on the flesh; if with flesh they make the maya of pleasure, painful deeds close round them; for those who have loved the Lord, release is like swimming across a river.
Three doors are kept shut and one is the door of sight; when the bolts of the shut doors open, see the sure Lord clearly within the flesh itself.

breath.reading: The three shut doors are the three knots on the central channel, or the three lower channels, and the one door of sight is the brow; opening them is the yogic ascent.

consciousness.reading: The Lord is seen in the flesh (மாங்கிசம்) that the previous verse warned against: the body is both the snare and the place of seeing.

literal.reading: That beginningless thing will be; if you seek and praise the feet of the One you may live as the child of Uma; the last line (வாகுடன் நீர்வன்னியை சமருவியே) does not construe with confidence.

breath.reading: நீர் and வன்னி, water and fire, would be the nectar and the root fire joined, if சமருவி is a form of joining.

literal.reading: If your devotion has ripened to the wish to be her child: there are four steps; kindle the fire in the root channel and drink that water, and through the lady of fragrant hair you reach the Lord's feet.

breath.reading: The fire kindled in the central channel and the water drunk are the raised kundalini and the nectar; Shakti is the way through to Siva.

literal.reading: If you bow and praise him with love, he removes death and birth; when the வாசி of the consort of the kohl-eyed lady climbs the sky, the strong deeds of the past scatter.

breath.reading: The breath, as practice, rising to the sky of the crown destroys past karma: love in the first half, breath in the second.

literal.reading: The Lord is known and seen when love melts within; if you drive the வாசி so that earth and sky shake, our Lord draws near and dwells in our sea.

breath.reading: Driving the breath is the practice named; the shaking of earth and sky is its sign, taken as the body's trembling.

consciousness.reading: 'Our sea' is the self or heart in which the Lord comes to dwell.

literal.reading: He (or the poet speaking as him) is in the count of eight by eight and becomes other; he becomes fire, air, water, earth and sky; those who have bathed in the guru's flood know by his mark the Lord of light who entered the womb and mingled with time.

breath.reading: எட்டெட்டு, sixty-four, is a count of the breath or of the tattvas; the text gives no key.

consciousness.reading: The Lord is the five elements and enters the womb: an immanence known only through the guru.

literal.reading: Jnanis who grasp the hint take it in their minds; those ripe for it gather it by praising with longing; the light that stands clear inside and outside, the awareness of awareness: realise its rightness.

consciousness.reading: The Lord is the awareness behind awareness, the same within and without.

literal.reading: Clear chariyai reaches salokam, kiriyai and puja samipam, yoga sarupam, and clear jnana, in all four, sayujyam.

The clear say one reaches jnana, but there is no reaching by the rightness of the four steps; those who reach Siva's state are those who received grace; seeing the way, make the four and your works firm.
The ignorant, not firm in the four steps, wander the land seeking, in vain; if you can show the mark and look within by it, you reach the true foot of the one with fragrant matted hair.

breath.reading: The குறி is the inner target of the gaze, which tradition places at the brow.

social.reading: Wandering the land on pilgrimage is the mark of the ignorant; the foot is reached by looking within.

literal.reading: You fools who do not know the release of those who reached: are not the tattvas with their army themselves the crimes? As the flow rises up the sluice when it is opened, raise the root channel in the body upward and plant it.

breath.reading: The practice is named outright: raise the root channel; the opened sluice pictures the sudden upward rush.

consciousness.reading: The tattvas, the body's constituents with their army, are what binds.

literal.reading: Planting and raising it, piercing the circle and opening the three bolts, if one mounts the channel the nectar comes down; the Lord appears to his servants and the soul joins the Supreme.

breath.reading: The ascent up the channel is followed by the descent of the nectar: that sequence is in the words. The circle and the three bolts are read, under keys, as the regions and the three knots.

consciousness.reading: The end is the soul joined to the Supreme, living there.

literal.reading: Raising the fire in the root channel with love, if the striving in infatuating maya ceases, then, like the Meru channel of thirst becoming many (obscure), those who bowed to the feet of the One will know.

breath.reading: Fire raised in the root channel; மேரு நாடி is the spinal channel.

consciousness.reading: The condition is the end of striving in maya.

literal.reading: Look within: the meditation is within you; to have the One's feet without being born again is true; line 3 does not construe cleanly; press on, open the upper door within you and look.

breath.reading: The upper door is the crown aperture, opened at the end of the ascent.

consciousness.reading: Release from rebirth is found by looking within.

literal.reading: If you can look clearly within as light, light rises and the song of turiya is reached; seated in the first chakra he bathes in holy water; see it without wavering, setting the breath right.

breath.reading: Correcting the breath is the one plain instruction; the first chakra is the root centre.

consciousness.reading: Light within and the fourth state, past waking, dream and sleep.

social.reading: The bath at the tirtha is relocated in the body; the verse does not attack the tank, but its neighbours do.

literal.reading: In the thought of the clear ones who became both Thiru and Siva, I become the fragrance that rises from the flower; the karma-traces carried from the womb, see, the fire consumes them like darkness before the sun.

consciousness.reading: The Lord (or the poet as him) is the fragrance in realised minds, and the traces of past deeds burn away.

literal.reading: Standing in the nature our father set, you reach the right thing by knowing the middle; Mal and Ayan, seeking the root and the crown, one digging the earth and one born into the sky, found nothing.

breath.reading: The middle is the central channel, between the root (வேர்) and the crown (முடி) that the two gods searched from outside.

literal.reading: You say for show that Ayan and Mal did not see him; can even a king be approached with insolence? If in service you worship with love, the devotion that burned the three cities will ripen.
It is complete: apart from him I see nothing before or after. What can hold the one that has no holding? Is it by learning that the Lord's feet are seen? Ask those who have gained them.

consciousness.reading: Only he is seen, nothing before or after; the one without holding is held only by not holding.

social.reading: Learning does not see the Lord's feet.

literal.reading: When the state you have heard of is gained, the wasting confusion of the tattvas goes; in the house it becomes open space and shines; joining fire and wind, it raises them from the breast (குயம், unclear).

breath.reading: Fire and breath joined and raised: the kindled breath of the chapter.

consciousness.reading: The attained state is open space shining within, with the tattvas' confusion gone.

literal.reading: Can one raise the root channel and make it easy? If you can draw in the assembly that does not deceive, passing beyond deep sleep and beyond dream, to settle in the one letter is the truth.

breath.reading: Raising the root channel, with a doubt about its ease.

consciousness.reading: Past deep sleep and dream to the fourth, settled in the one letter, which tradition takes as Om.

links.note: Tirumular says they wander everywhere in the land seeking Nandi, who is fragrant within the body, and do not know the purpose that stands in the body; Sivavakkiyar asks where they run saying 'he is not in this town' and places the Lord in the six centres within.

Before the key, Sivavakkiyar places the Lord 'in the final சி and அ' and Agappei says 'the letter சி is the root'. Under the five-syllable key, சி is Siva in both, so both make the syllable சி the place or source of the Lord. The pairing shows a single letter-key running across two poets; it holds only if Sivavakkiyar's சீயில் அவ்வில் names letters at all, which is not certain.

Both give the Siddhanta pairing of paths and fruits: Tirumular has salokam and samipam from sariyai and sarupam as the way to the formless Supreme; Sivavakkiyar lays out all four, chariyai to salokam, kiriyai to samipam, yoga to sarupam and jnana to sayujyam.

1400 states the four paths with their four fruits as a ladder; 1401 says there is no reaching by the rightness of the four steps, and that those who reach Siva's state are those who received grace, then tells them to make the four firm. Grace becomes the cause and the paths its expression.

Sivavakkiyar says raise the root channel in the body upward, as water rushes up an opened sluice; Arunagirinathar asks that the breath, run from the root through the left and right channels, go up the pillar from the root through the six centres. Both name the practice in plain technical words (மூல நாடி, மூலம், பிங்கலை, தூண்), so the link needs no key; the Siddhar gives it as an order to fools, the Thiruppugazh as a prayer to Murugan.

Both give one sequence: raise from the root, and nectar follows. Tirumular says the seed in the root, led by the fire there, is raised above the throat and becomes cool nectar at the moon; Sivavakkiyar says plant and raise, mount the channel, and the nectar comes down (அமுதம் வந்து இறங்கிடும்). The ascent and the nectar are in both Tamil texts. Sivavakkiyar's circle and three bolts are not matched in Tirumular, and this link does not rest on them.

1395 gives the two ends of the practice: kindle the fire in the root channel and drink 'that water'. 1404 supplies the route between them: plant and raise, pierce the circle, open the three bolts, mount the channel, and the nectar comes down. The fire-and-water pair is named in 1395 and the nectar in 1404, so the development is in the words; the three bolts are the only keyed term.

Before the key, Sivavakkiyar says 'open the upper door within you and look', and Idaikkadar tells the herdsman to know the sight of the lotus in the head. Under the upper-door key, Sivavakkiyar's door is the crown aperture, which Idaikkadar names plainly as சிரம், the head; both make the top of the body the place where the Lord is seen. Idaikkadar fixes the place, and Sivavakkiyar needs the key to reach it.

Both use the myth of the gods who could not find Siva's limits: Arunagirinathar names Vishnu on the serpent who could not find the feet in the depth of the netherworld, Sivavakkiyar has Mal dig the earth and Ayan fly the sky for the root and the crown and find nothing. Sivavakkiyar adds the lesson, know the middle.

The Kural says cling to the clinging of the one without clinging in order to let clinging go; Sivavakkiyar asks what can hold on to the one that has no holding, and answers that learning cannot, only asking those who have reached. The paradox is the same; the Kural treats it as method, Sivavakkiyar as a question about who can teach it.

Both define the knowing of the Real by doubling the knower's own word: Sivavakkiyar's light is 'awareness to awareness' (உணர்வதற்கு உணர்வு), Idaikkadar's herdsman holds 'truth in truth' and goes on in true knowledge (மெய்யே மெய்யில் கொண்டு மெய்யறிவில்). Two poets reach for the same reflexive formula for a knowing that has no outside object; Sivavakkiyar adds that it is the same within and without.

Sivavakkiyar calls those who wander the land seeking (தேசநாடி அலைவது) ignorant and says the true foot is reached by looking within at the mark; Konganar's kummi has the dancer's lifted foot inside you and asks why go to Chidambaram. Beyond the shared attack on pilgrimage, both end in the same object, the Lord's foot seen within, which is what replaces the journey.

old_links.note: Holds on the plain first two lines; the coded last line is support only, as the grader said.
Both state the path-fruit scheme in plain words.
The note missed that Agappei grants chariyai its salokam; the pair is kept the other way round as 1666 qualifies 1400.
Adjacent verses; the qualification is in the words.
The two set aside different things (three fruits against the four paths' rightness); only 'above the scheme' is shared.

The ascent-then-nectar sequence is in both texts; the old note leaned on the cipher terms of 1404 (circle, three bolts) as if they matched Tirumular's throat and moon. Renoted on the breath layer, resting only on the named sequence.
God as the five elements is the commonest Saiva claim; the pairing teaches nothing specific.
The same myth in both, with Sivavakkiyar's lesson.
The same paradox in the same word பற்று.
The note's 'direct seeing' fits Tirumular only; Sivavakkiyar's alternative is to ask those who have attained.
The inner tirtha extends 1357's body-as-shrine; holds on the plain words. 1357 is outside the pilot.
Valmiki maps the breath phases onto the four paths in plain words; holds without a key.
Both state that the lower paths need jnana; plain words.
1400 itself gives yoga only sarupam, so the tension with Agappei's denial of yoga holds only on a misreading of 1400.

source_issues: 1391 line 2: தொக்கு is Sanskrit tvak, skin, so the line lists four senses (skin, eye, tongue, nose); the flat marks read it as 'gathered'.
1394 line 4, 1402 line 1, 1405 line 3 and 1406 lines 1 and 3 do not construe with confidence (as the flat marks also record).
